description: This line plot illustrates the average number of shared Top-6 routed experts across two independent samples for six different tasks—Intent, Summary, Law, Translation, Code, and Math—as a function of sample token count. The x-axis, labeled “Sample Token Count,” is logarithmic, spanning from 2^9 (512) to 2^20 (1,048,576), with tick marks at powers of two. The y-axis, labeled “Shared Experts for Two Samples,” ranges from 2.0 to 6.0 and represents the average number of shared experts across model layers. The orange line for “Intent” starts at approximately 3.7 at 2^9 and rises to about 6.0 at 2^20. The blue line for “Summary” begins at 2.0 at 2^9, sharply increases to a peak of 4.7 at 2^12, then declines to 4.5 at 2^14 before rising again to 5.8 at 2^20. The yellow line for “Law” starts at 3.6 at 2^9, peaks at 5.7 at 2^13, then declines slightly to 5.5 at 2^15 before stabilizing near 6.0. The purple line for “Translation” begins at 5.1 at 2^9, rises to 5.7 at 2^13, and remains near 6.0 from 2^15 to 2^20. The gray line for “Code” starts at 2.0 at 2^9, rises to 3.7 at 2^11, peaks at 3.8 at 2^13, dips to 3.1 at 2^14, and then steadily increases to 5.7 at 2^20. The green line for “Math” begins at 3.8 at 2^9, rises to 4.7 at 2^12, then climbs to a peak of 6.0 at 2^18 before slightly declining to 5.9 at 2^20.
